title: Ray-Ban Meta Creates First Audio-Only Glasses Amid Online Discussions Over Camera Recording & Privacy
summary: The new glasses are for those who want all the audio and microphone features without the built-in camera.
contentText:

The public spoke, and Ray-Ban Meta appears to have heard them. As camera-equipped smart glasses become more common, some wearers have found that the built-in camera recording feature can create an awkward social dynamic, with people around them questioning whether they are being recorded or feeling uneasy about the possibility. Online discussions have also seen users express interest in having Ray-Ban Meta’s popular audio features for music , podcasts and calls without a camera at all. For these listeners, an audio-only option offers a simpler way to enjoy hands-free music, podcasts and calls while keeping the focus strictly on listening rather than capturing content.

Now, the brand is launching Ray-Ban Meta Audio , its first audio-only AI glasses. Built around open-ear audio, the new frames let users listen to music and podcasts, take calls and access Meta AI without reaching for their phone. For music lovers , that means keeping a personal soundtrack playing throughout the day while staying aware of their surroundings. Ray-Ban Meta Audio is available to preorder Sept. 23 and officially arrives Oct. 13.

Ray-Ban Meta Audio brings open-ear listening, Meta AI and an everyday Ray-Ban design together in the brand’s lightest smart glasses frame yet. Weighing 43 grams, the glasses are built for extended listening, with up to 12 hours of battery life for music, podcasts, calls and hands-free access to Meta AI. The open-ear setup lets listeners enjoy audio while staying connected to their surroundings, making the glasses a natural fit for commutes, walks and everyday routines.

The new audio-first experience arrives in two distinctive Ray-Ban silhouettes: Clubmaster and Burbank. Clubmaster draws from the browline styles that became defining looks of the 1950s and 1960s, while Burbank revisits a square acetate design originally introduced in the ’60s and brought back from the Ray-Ban archive in 2021. Both frames blend vintage-inspired styling with modern audio and AI capabilities.

Alongside Ray-Ban Meta Audio , Ray-Ban is also launching its next-generation camera-equipped glasses today. Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 3) introduces slimmer designs across Wayfarer, Aviator and Zena, plus a 3K Ultra HD camera, upgraded six-microphone array, customizable action button and up to nine hours of battery life. The Aviator joins the collection for the first time, including a limited-edition Milky Warm Beige version, while Meta AI adds hands-free tools for everything from real-time translations and reminders to music, messaging and taking photos.
